label: TP
reason: User-controlled input from request.getParameter() flows through doSomething() via HashMap storage/retrieval and ends up concatenated directly into SQL query string without parameterization. The SQL injection vulnerability is real - attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the 'BenchmarkTest02180' parameter. Note: Error handling uses encodeForHTML() for EmptyResultDataAccessException but this only protects error messages, not the main query path.

evidence.note: User input extracted from HTTP request parameter
User input stored in HashMap and retrieved - no sanitization occurs
